Accepted, and it coalesces: PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 proposes the same roadmap with the byte-identical id and title, which is the natural pairing since that paper is about anabelian geometry with etale homotopy types and this one needs the same machinery for Appendix A. The appendix findings travel with it, and they matter for the brief: E14 shows that the comparison criterion needs degreewise finite-dimensional F_p-cohomology and that for the infinite coproducts used here Et_p must be taken componentwise, and E16 that a smooth surjection need not have smooth target.

Part II of K-theory of number fields and S-integers, 36 items. Accepted. The title is an exact prefix extension of 'K-theory of number fields and S-integers' and the id is free. The mathematics is genuinely a new layer in that roadmap's direction rather than a restatement of it: symplectic K-theory KSp_*(Z) as the K-theory of the category of symplectic lattices, its relation to ordinary K-theory through the hyperbolic and forgetful maps, the CM abelian varieties that produce classes, the exhaustion theorem, and the Galois action with its Iwasawa-theoretic identification. The parent owns the K-theory of number rings, which this imports through route 2 and through fifteen planned items rather than re-planning. Two findings bear on what the brief must state: E10, which shows the divisibility theorem is proved for p > max_j(n_j) rather than the printed p >= max_j(n_j), and E12, which shows the Postnikov-splitting step of Theorem 8.4 needs another argument.

notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, for issue 1267, 23 September 2026. Verdict: accept.

SOURCE, WITH A LIMITATION. The paper is open access, and the extraction records the published PDF's SHA-256. As with every Springer-published paper I have reviewed today, that hash could not be re-verified here: the PDF endpoint returns a JavaScript challenge page to every request. I read the published text through a rendering proxy instead and rebuilt the journal page map from the running heads - 94 marks running from p. 226 to p. 319, consistent with the stated 225-319 - and checked every finding at its recorded page. Crossref records no correction.

MISTAKES. All 17 findings were checked at their locators and all 17 are confirmed. The record is careful: fifteen are classified as affecting nothing and they genuinely do not, one is a gap in a proof, and one reaches a stated result.

Several are settled by the paper against itself. E5 is not even well typed as printed - the objects of the category are triples (V, pi, s) with pi : V -> M and s : M -> V, so 's o pi = id_M' is an endomorphism of V, and the short exact sequence displayed immediately after draws s as a section of pi. E6's exponent is fixed by the line above it, which reads beta^{2k-1}. E9's 'Theorem 3.3' does not exist; (3.3) is the Betti-Hodge map of Theorem 3.5. E11's 'integral indecomposables' names a quotient that Example 8.3 itself computes as I/(I^2 + beta_1(I_1^2)). E17's Rosati condition is circular as printed.

E10 IS THE ONE THAT REACHES A STATED RESULT, and the paper's own introduction corroborates it. Theorem 8.1 claims divisibility for each prime p >= max_j(n_j), but the argument caps with ch_{n_j}(omega) = s_{n_j}/n_j!, which needs Z_(p)-integrality, and that fails exactly at n_j = p: the Adams summand is a retract of KSp(Z)^p by Theorem 3.5, so the class with <ch_p, b_p> = 1/p! lifts and ch_p is not p-integral on A_g for large g. The distinguished index cannot be p, since p never divides the numerator of B_{p+1} by Kummer's congruence, but another part can be, and the introduction's one-part version already says 'in the range when p > 2k'. The boundary case is unproved, not disproved, and the finding says exactly that.

E12 is a real gap in an argument, honestly reported. The deloop's k-invariant P^1 : K(Z/p,2) -> K(Z/p,2p) connects pi_1(X) to pi_{2p-2}(X), inside the truncation range, so tau_{<=2p-2}X need not split as a product of Eilenberg-MacLane loop spaces; alpha_1 in pi_{2p-3}(S), detected by P^1, is the standard witness. The finding adds that the conclusion of Theorem 8.4 is not contradicted there - the Hurewicz image of alpha_1 survives in the indecomposables - so what fails is the argument, not the theorem. That distinction is what makes the record usable.

ITEMS AND ROUTES. 57 items: 1 library, 15 planned, 41 missing, each missing item routed exactly once, all dependencies resolving. The seven declarations behind the single library item were opened at the pinned commits. All twenty-six stage ids cited by the routes and the planned items exist, including the three Tau Ceti layer anchors. Five routes, all accepted; the Part II title is an exact prefix extension and both proposed ids are free. The new roadmap EtaleHomotopyTypes is co-proposed byte-identically by PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16, the natural partner, so the two coalesce on one design job.
